A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text and complete Appendices A–M. Text comparison and visual inspection support matching the methods, equations, tables and figures across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original FTCT experiments comparing Transformers and MLPs, attention and probing analyses, and appendix experiments on robustness and larger models.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised probing scores and larger-model performance curves.

M1.justification: The FTCT generation procedure, prompting, training objectives, underlying reasoning program and Transformer construction remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and the corresponding appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic FTCT task coverage, including noisy inputs, varying chain lengths and incomplete intermediate reasoning. The additional configuration in Figure 8 extends an existing parameter sweep rather than introducing distinct task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Transformer layer/head variants and two- and four-layer MLPs. Appendix J retains GPT-2-small and GPT-2-large; no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Figure 8 newly includes a GPT-2-large series for depth 13 with child-chain length 6, extending the reported experimental configurations. Existing metric definitions and stated training/probing protocols remain unchanged; no protocol revision explains the other changed scores.

E4.justification: The additional depth-13, child-length-6 condition in Figure 8 modestly extends the GPT-2-large sensitivity analysis of training fragment length. The noise, shortened-chain, incomplete-step and mechanistic analyses otherwise retain their designs.

E5.justification: Figures 6–9 newly display shaded uncertainty bands. Both versions already report averaging over five causal structures and standard deviations in Appendix H.1, but Appendix J does not specify the new bands' definition or disclose additional run/seed counts.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces the depth-15/child-5 probing scores: zero-shot and four-shot test Parent accuracy change from 55.4 and 35.9 to 78.2 and 73.9. Figures 6–9 substantially revise larger-model curves; for example, Figure 6's GPT-2-small depth-10/child-3 two-shot whole accuracy changes from approximately 0.08 to 0.69. These sizeable revisions alter the reported empirical evidence under the same labeled configurations, although their cause is unexplained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Lemmas 5.1–5.3, Theorem 5.4 and constructions/proofs in Appendices D–F are unchanged. Appendix E only has a renumbered footnote.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims about few-shot CoT, training/testing similarity, multi-layer attention and learning an underlying generalizable program. Revised results do not produce revised core claims.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations, proposed explanation for deterioration with additional shots, larger-model overfitting hypothesis, and limitations concerning natural-language applicability and missing intermediate steps remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page footnote identifying a GitHub code repository, providing access information absent from v1. The data-generation and implementation details in Appendices B and G are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and research positioning in Section 2 remain unchanged. The added code link does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: The new code footnote accompanies changed author-affiliation markers, subsequent footnote renumbering and updated arXiv header text. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 6–9 are updated with shaded bands, and Figure 8 includes an additional series, while retaining their panel organization and captions. The code footnote slightly changes first-page layout; Table 3 retains its structure despite numerical revisions.

improvement.justification: The added code-access information and newly visualized uncertainty in Figures 6–9 modestly improve transparency. However, Appendix J does not define the bands or explain the substantial result revisions, limiting their evidential benefit. Higher revised accuracies alone do not establish improved paper quality.
